items.paraphrased_contract: Account for the explicit StandardML suspension extension: syntax and typing, fresh thunk allocation, body evaluation and memoization before inner matching, effectful matching and exception propagation, recursive environment updates and the separately tracked pure self-reentry claim. A body exception adds no successful write at that frame; a failed inner match can follow a successful cache write.
items.cost_mode: operational/static semantics; supplies assumptions for later resource claims
notes: This is distinct from book Appendix A, which supplies Haskell implementations.

The appendix states modifications to the external Standard ML Definition; full union coverage must delimit the modeled base fragment and explicitly account for every added/modified rule, not silently claim a full Standard ML implementation.
Recursive self-forcing can memoize more than once in the presence of side effects; optional blackhole detection is discussed as an alternative, not specified as mandatory behavior.
The effectful examples are semantic tests even though the primary data-structure programs are purely functional.
The p135 pure self-forcing nontermination remark is an explicit additional proof obligation TU.A.4.PURE under local10019, required before complete AppendixA/Chapter4 acceptance.

items.paraphrased_contract: Construct the sketched segmented binomial random-access lists and heaps using real-time deques for segments and child sequences, bulk linking/unlinking and the minimum-root-at-smallest-tree invariant. For the list, cons/head/tail have constant worst-case cost and lookup/update logarithmic cost; for the heap, insert has constant worst-case cost and merge/findMin/deleteMin logarithmic cost.
items.cost_mode: worst-case under primitive real-time deque and unit-cost assumptions
notes: Book9.2.4 and Exercises9.11-9.13 discuss segmented/redundant numerical representations but do not identify this same bulk-link construction.
The thesis gives a design sketch and bounds, not complete executable code; completion requires making the design concrete and proving the stated contracts.

items.paraphrased_contract: Implement and analyze the thesis lazy redundant numeral system with digits1,2,3, where2 is safe and1/3 are dangerous, supporting mixed increment/decrement sequences in constant amortized cost.
items.cost_mode: amortized with one debit on the tail of a safe digit and none on a dangerous-digit tail
notes: Book9.2.3 pp126-127 uses digits0,1,2 with safe1. The numeral-value encodings differ; a constructor rename is insufficient as a correspondence proof.
Retain the counterexample for alternating ordinary binary increment/decrement and the incompatibility of the separate debit invariants.

items.paraphrased_contract: Prove the scheduled binary-digit increment realization maintains completed-zero separation of pending ranges and consequently takes constant worst-case cost.
notes: Book7.3 Theorem7.1 uses the analogous range-separation invariant for scheduled binomial heaps; a common generic proof still needs checked instantiations for both representations.
Thesis8.2 also gives an unscheduled lazy binary increment and its amortized theorem8.1.

items.paraphrased_contract: Preserve the distinction between delaying pattern matching and forcing arguments before constructing a suspended result, including the take examples and the deliberately one-level-ahead digit increment. Connect book fun-lazy notation to its explicit desugaring.
items.cost_mode: demand/evaluation behavior plus the owning algorithms resource claims
notes: Book4.1 pp32-33 supplies fun-lazy sugar; the thesis uses explicit suspensions and a case expression.
Extensional equality of fully forced finite results alone does not establish the intended forcing or cost correspondence.

items.paraphrased_contract: Model execution traces with the source allowances for cycles, parallel edges, multiple arguments/results and distinct persistent identities. Formalize fresh debit allocation and logical-history discharge/realization conditions, and bound the union of realized debits by the sum of discharge multiset cardinalities.
items.cost_mode: aggregate actual-versus-amortized bound with memoized realized cost
notes: A DAG-only or single-version-path model does not by itself cover this trace scope.
The source labels s(v) with sets and a(v),r(v) with multisets. The cost of realized work counts each memoized debit once; discharge may be counted repeatedly across logical futures.
This is shared with book6, not necessarily new book-exclusive mathematics, but the union ledger must preserve the precise assumptions.

items.paraphrased_contract: Account for nonuniform recursive representations and the translation to uniform Standard ML forms, and for the generic higher-order recursive heap bootstrap transformation with its primitive interface/cost assumptions.
items.cost_mode: semantic correspondence and conditional worst-case/amortized transfer
notes: A single concrete bootstrapped heap does not automatically cover the generic transformation.
The thesis explicitly excludes effectful primitive functors from the intended recursive-module pattern; do not generalize beyond those assumptions.
Book10 overlaps this material, including explicit exercises for alternative queue realizations.

items.paraphrased_contract: Account for two constant-amortized variants beyond the log-star bootstrapped queue: suspend the recursive middle queue and execute all its operations lazily; or use a two-level stream of suspended lists with incremental append and amortize its cost over top-level queue operations.
items.cost_mode: amortized O(1) for the claimed queue operations under explicit laziness/debt assumptions
notes: Book10.1.3 Exercise10.5 gives a primitive-queue functor and a real-time-primitive hypothesis. That does not automatically discharge these specific thesis variants.
The second variation is described rather than fully coded and points to a separate paper; formalize the stated sketch or record any required external detail before claiming parity.

items.paraphrased_contract: In a properly specified pure source domain, an evaluation that forces its own still-pending suspension cannot have a finite completion. Stronger successful memoization bounds must follow from proved client restrictions.
